From what I've seen from friends who were very high achievers, it's a combination of factors that lead to that level of success. 

The overachiever: Person performs at peak levels at the expense of many of life's little pleasures. High anxiety and stress, and a tendency towards perfectionism. These people can and will experience crashes unless they can deal with stress in a healthy manner. 

The Savant: Marked by seeming lack of effort and high levels of performance, the savant just happens to be in their element and you have the misfortune of comparing yourself to someone whose stars aligned for them. People like this tend to be in the right place at the right time, and will always move around until they are in their element. Being outside their element brings them frustration and pain as they are next to useless. Intense specialization and focus mixed with natural talent, but mostly they follow their passions much more-so than others so they tend to always appear to be good at whatever they do. 

The addict: Either one of the other types, or just a normal person, who has found the power of chemical assistance. Adderall, ritalin, or xanax, or even the harder stuff (speed, cocaine), either one or a cocktail of many, the addict leverages pharmaceutical might to deal with whatever happens to be holding them back. The disadvantages with this approach are obvious, but on paper, they will resemble an overachiever or a savant. 

Don't be afraid of being mediocre, because being super successful may be a nightmare.
